purpose:
This policy says how {{HOSPITAL_NAME}} meets NABH Hospitals 6th Edition standard COP.18: Rehabilitation services are provided to the patients in a safe, collaborative and consistent manner.

It covers objective elements COP.18.a–g (7 elements).

This policy owns COP.18. Related AAC, PRE, IPC/HIC, HRM and MOM duties stay with those policies — cross-reference only.

Words marked «like this» are defaults. A blank marked «________» must be filled before issue.
scope:
This policy applies to staff who deliver or oversee the care described in COP.18 at {{HOSPITAL_NAME}}, including the «Rehabilitation In-Charge», treating doctors, nurses and the Quality Coordinator.

It covers 7 objective elements (COP.18.a, COP.18.b, COP.18.c, COP.18.d, COP.18.e, COP.18.f, COP.18.g).

Boundaries: do not copy SHCO COP wording. Do not overwrite AAC policies. Spell out abbreviations on first use in training materials.
policy_statement:
{{HOSPITAL_NAME}} implements COP.18 so that rehabilitation services are provided to the patients in a safe, collaborative and consistent manner..

Staff follow written guidance, keep the records listed in the OE table, and escalate when stop-work triggers fire (if this policy includes a stop-work section).
procedure_steps:
5.1 Scope of the rehabilitation services at a minimum is commensurate to ..

Scope of the rehabilitation services at a minimum is commensurate to the services provided by the organisation.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.2 Rehabilitation services are provided in a consistent manner

Rehabilitation services are provided in a consistent manner.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.3 Care providers collaboratively plan rehabilitation services

Care providers collaboratively plan rehabilitation services.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.4 There are adequate space and equipment to provide rehabilitation

There are adequate space and equipment to provide rehabilitation.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.5 Care is guided by functional assessment and periodic re-assessments w..

Care is guided by functional assessment and periodic re-assessments which are done and documented.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.6 Care is provided adhering to infection prevention and control and saf..

Care is provided adhering to infection prevention and control and safety practices.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.

5.7 Care pathways are developed, implemented, and reviewed periodically

Care pathways are developed, implemented, and reviewed periodically.

Staff follow the written guidance and record the action in the medical record or the department register named for this element.
responsibility:
Medical Superintendent
- Accountable that COP.18 is resourced and followed.

Rehabilitation In-Charge
- Owns day-to-day implementation and records for this standard.

Treating doctors / nurses / technicians (as applicable)
- Deliver care as written; escalate stop-work triggers without delay.

Quality Coordinator
- Audits this policy «quarterly»; holds training acknowledgements.

The requirements in this document are accreditation requirements of the NABH Full Accreditation Standards for Hospitals, 6th Edition, not duties under a named Act of Parliament. The clinical and technical content reflects recognised national and international guidance current at the date of preparation. {{HOSPITAL_NAME}} remains responsible for verifying that it is current and consistent with the edition of the accreditation standard against which it is being assessed.

This document is not issued by, endorsed by, or affiliated with NABH, the World Health Organization, the National Centre for Disease Control, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, any Pollution Control Board, or any other body named in it. monitoring_audit:
The Quality Coordinator audits this policy «quarterly».

What is monitored each quarter:

- Sample of records for each OE COP.18.a–g.
- Asterisked elements (none) have document evidence as required.
- CORE elements (none) show no critical gaps in the sample.
- Stop-work events (if any) are logged with outcome.

This policy is reviewed «annually», and sooner after a related adverse event.
training_competency:
Staff covered by this policy are trained at induction and «once a year» after that. Training covers the What-we-do steps, non-negotiables and stop-work (if present).
